title: Casting the restricted weight estimate
statement: Let $n,a,b,s$ be natural numbers with $0<n$, $0<a$, $2a\le b$, and $1\le s$. Consider the restricted-weight input specified by dimension $n$, bias numerator $a$, bias denominator $b$, and Fourier bound $s$. For any coordinate set $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, any $S\subseteq J$, and any assignment of signs to the queries in the associated finite query set, the rational estimate obtained by averaging the squared inner sample averages over the outer samples, divided by the outer sample count, equals the corresponding real-valued estimate.
hypotheses_covered: Twice the bias numerator is at most the bias denominator: $2a\le b$
